questions.tip: Use your self-appraisal: name, LGA and state, date of birth, schools, achievements, work experience. 60–90 seconds. End with one line on why you are here today.
questions.model: Good morning. My name is ___, from ___ Local Government Area of ___ State, born on ___. I attended ___ and graduated from ___ with ___. During ___ I ___ (an achievement). I have worked as ___, where I learned ___. I am here because I want to put these skills to work protecting Nigeria's interests.

questions.q: Why do you want to join the National Intelligence Agency?
questions.tip: Show purpose, not just salary. Link to national service, your interest in world affairs, and your skills.
questions.model: I want a career where my work directly protects Nigeria. I follow international affairs closely, especially the Sahel and the Middle East, and I understand how events abroad reach our borders. The Agency is where that interest becomes service.

questions.q: What is your vision? What will you contribute to the Agency?
questions.tip: Name 2–3 concrete strengths (languages, analysis, IT, research, people skills) and link each to the Agency's mission. Show you want to grow through training.
questions.model: I see myself becoming a reliable analyst and officer the Agency can trust with sensitive work. I bring ___ and ___. Within five years I want to have mastered ___ and to be contributing to how Nigeria understands threats in our region.

questions.q: What do you know about the NIA?
questions.tip: Created 1986 from the NSO, alongside the DSS and DIA. Handles foreign intelligence and counter-intelligence. Coordinated through the National Security Adviser. DG: Amb. Mohammed Mohammed. Stop there; don't speculate about operations.
questions.model: The NIA was created in 1986 when the National Security Organisation was split into three agencies. It is responsible for Nigeria's security outside the country on non-military matters, gathering foreign intelligence and protecting our interests abroad.

questions.q: What are your strengths and weaknesses?
questions.tip: Give a real weakness with what you are doing about it. Avoid “I work too hard”.
questions.model: My strength is ___, for example ___. A weakness is that I ___; I've been working on it by ___, and it has improved.

questions.q: What is the biggest security threat facing Nigeria today?
questions.tip: Pick one, justify it, and show you see links between threats (Sahel spillover, banditry, terrorism financing). Mention a policy angle.
questions.model: I'd say the spread of armed groups across the Sahel into the North-west, because it combines terrorism, banditry and smuggling and exploits the gap between Nigeria's security system and the AES states. Rebuilding cooperation with Niger is essential.

questions.q: What is your view on the Alliance of Sahel States leaving ECOWAS?
questions.tip: Be balanced and diplomatic. Facts first (2023 charter, January 2025 exit), then impact on Nigeria, then what Nigeria should do.
questions.model: It weakens regional security cooperation at the worst time. Nigeria should keep supporting constitutional rule but also keep practical security and trade links with Niger, because terrorists don't respect borders.

questions.q: Tell us about the Russia–Ukraine war.
questions.tip: Start date, current state, peace efforts, effect on Nigeria (food and fuel prices), Nigeria's position (sovereignty, UN Charter).
questions.model: Russia invaded on 24 February 2022 after annexing Crimea in 2014. The fighting is now slow, along the eastern front. The US has pushed peace proposals, but Russia's demand for all of Donbas is the sticking point. For Nigeria, it raised wheat, fertiliser and fuel prices.

questions.q: What is happening between the US, Israel and Iran?
questions.tip: February 2026 start, Hormuz, Pakistan's role, Qatar now mediating, oil impact on Nigeria.
questions.model: War began in February 2026 when US and Israeli strikes killed Iran's Supreme Leader. Iran closed the Strait of Hormuz. Pakistan brokered a memorandum and a ceasefire in June, but it collapsed in July. Qatar is now carrying indirect talks. For Nigeria, oil prices and shipping costs are the immediate effects.

questions.q: You are asked to keep something secret from your family. How do you handle it?
questions.tip: Show you understand discretion as part of the job, and that you can do it without lying in a harmful way.
questions.model: I would keep it confidential. My family would know I can't discuss work, and I would set that expectation early so it isn't a source of tension.

questions.q: A colleague is leaking information. What do you do?
questions.tip: Integrity and chain of command: report through the proper channel, don't investigate alone, don't gossip.
questions.model: I would report it through the proper channel to my superior without delay. Loyalty to the Agency and the country comes before personal friendship.
I stay calm by breaking the problem into steps. For example, when ___, I ___ and we delivered on time.

questions.q: Where do you see yourself in five years?
questions.tip: Growth inside the Agency, training, specialisation. Ambitious but realistic.
questions.model: Fully trained, trusted with responsibility, and specialised in ___, while still learning.

questions.q: What do you understand by Nigeria's 4-D foreign policy?
questions.tip: Democracy, Development, Demography, Diaspora, with one example each.
questions.model: It's the government's foreign policy framework: defending democracy in the region, using diplomacy for economic development, turning our young population into an asset, and engaging Nigerians abroad.

questions.q: Do you speak any foreign languages?
questions.tip: Be honest. If you are learning French or Arabic, say so: they are very relevant to West Africa and the Sahel.
questions.model: I speak ___ and ___. I've started learning ___ because it's widely used in our neighbouring countries.

questions.q: Do you have any questions for us?
questions.tip: Always have one. Ask about training or what makes officers succeed. Don't ask about salary first.
questions.model: What qualities do the most successful officers in the Agency share?

questions.q: What is human trafficking and how does it affect Nigeria?
questions.tip: Definition, NAPTIP 2003, the 2015 Act, routes via Niger and Libya, link to organised crime.
questions.model: Moving or holding people by force or deception to exploit them. Nigeria is a source, transit and destination country. NAPTIP enforces the 2015 Act. Routes through Niger and Libya overlap with smuggling and terrorist networks.

questions.q: Tell us about the security situation in your state.
questions.tip: Know your own state and zone well: main threats, recent incidents, what government is doing. Be factual, not political.
questions.model: In ___ State the main concern is ___. Recently ___. The government has responded with ___, though challenges remain in ___.
